meaning: the son of the heir; a variant of Ayre or Eyre with the patronymic s suffixed
author_comment: No doubt a variant of Ayre or Eyre, q.v., with the patronymic s suffixed, as in Jones, Simmons, Roberts, &c. Therefore literally 'the son of the heir.' My first instance seems to set the matter at rest. Several families of Ayres or Aires went out to America in the 17th century, which fact accounts for its familiar recurrence in the United States; v. index, Hotten's Lists of Emigrants.
source: Allegations for Marriage Licences issued by the Bishop of London, 1520-1828 (Harleian Society), p. 325
record_text: 1610. Hugh Jones and Eliz. Ayres: Marriage Lic. (London), p. 325.
